name: number-field
title: Number field
purpose: A numeric input as the control of a field, with an optional unit written beside it and optional stepper buttons.
whenToUse: For an amount the reader types or nudges: a timeout in minutes, a retry count, a spending limit.
With stepper buttons when the value is small and usually changes by a step or two.
With a unit whenever the number alone could be misread.
whenNotToUse: For a number that is a name, such as a run number, a port or a one-time code. Use a field with inputmode="numeric", or the one-time-code input.
For a rough amount where the exact figure does not matter. Use a slider.
For one of a few fixed amounts. Use a select or a radio group.
For a date or a time. Use a date field.

variants.name: with a unit
variants.use: A span with gw-number-field__unit after the input, holding the unit as a word.

variants.name: with steppers
variants.use: Two icon buttons with gw-number-field__step at the end of the row: decrease first, then increase.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 44px tall and at most 264px wide. Each stepper is 44px square.

accessibility: Use input type="number" carrying gw-field__control and gw-number-field__input, inside a div with gw-number-field, inside gw-field. The label, description and error are the field's.
Set min, max and step on the input, and say the range in the description. Set inputmode="numeric" for whole numbers and inputmode="decimal" when step is a fraction, so a phone shows the right keys.
Write the unit as a word in a span with gw-number-field__unit, give it an id and list that id first in the input's aria-describedby, so a screen reader hears Run timeout, 30, minutes.

A stepper is a button with type="button" and the classes gw-button, gw-icon-button and gw-number-field__step, holding the minus or plus icon with aria-hidden="true" and a gw-visually-hidden name that says what it changes and by how much, such as Increase the run timeout by 5 minutes.
The app wires the steppers: on a press it calls stepDown() or stepUp() on the input and dispatches an input event. It sets disabled on the decrease button at min and on the increase button at max.
The Up and Down arrow keys step the value while the input has focus. That comes from the input, and the browser's own small spin buttons are hidden.
For a value out of range, set aria-invalid="true" on the input and link a gw-field__error that repeats the value and gives the limit.
When the input is disabled, set disabled on both steppers too.
